intro: You're looking for a landlord accountant near you because your rental income needs proper handling, whether it's a single property or a growing portfolio. You want someone local who understands the tax rules that apply to landlords and can help you keep more of what you earn. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK accountant who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a landlord accountant near me usually need
need_lead: Most landlords want an accountant who can take the worry out of rental accounts and tax, while keeping everything above board.
needs: You own one or more rental properties and need help preparing rental income accounts that are accurate and complete.
You're unsure which expenses you can claim against rental income and want to make sure you're not missing allowable costs.
You've heard about the restrictions on mortgage interest relief and want to understand how they affect your tax position.
You're thinking about buying or selling property through a limited company and need advice on whether incorporation makes sense for you.
You want to stay on top of Making Tax Digital for landlords and need someone who can guide you through the changes.
context_heading: What to understand about landlord accountants near you
context: In the UK, the word "accountant" on its own is not a protected title, so anyone can call themselves an accountant. However, titles such as Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant are protected, and members are bound by their professional body's ethics, training and complaints rules. It's reasonable to ask which professional body supervises the firm and whether they hold professional indemnity insurance.

Every accountancy practice offering services must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC. When you speak to a landlord accountant, you can ask about their experience with rental property accounts and whether they are familiar with Making Tax Digital for landlords. iComply does not give advice or take responsibility for any professional's work; we simply introduce you to someone who can quote you directly.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: How many rental properties you own and whether they are held personally or through a limited company.
The type of rental income you receive, such as residential, commercial or furnished holiday lets.
Whether you have any particular concerns, like mortgage interest relief or Making Tax Digital.
If you already keep records for each property and how you currently manage your accounts.
Whether you need help with a one-off tax return or ongoing accountancy support.
Your preferred location or whether you are happy to work with an accountant remotely.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the landlord accountant
questions: What experience do you have with landlord accounts and rental property tax?
Which professional body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you handle the restriction on mortgage interest relief for landlords?
Can you explain how Making Tax Digital for landlords will affect me?
What records should I keep for each property to make your job easier?

faqs.q: Do I need a specialist landlord accountant?
faqs.a: A specialist landlord accountant can help you navigate the specific rules for rental income, such as allowable expenses and mortgage interest restrictions. If you have multiple properties or complex affairs, their expertise can be particularly valuable.

faqs.q: What does 'price on application' mean for accountant fees?
faqs.a: It means the accountant will quote you a fee based on your individual circumstances after you discuss your needs. iComply does not set fees; the professional you are introduced to will provide a personalised quote.
